title: Colours

parent.learn: Names of the main colours: red, blue, yellow, green, orange, purple, pink, black, white, brown.
parent.why: Colour words help describe and sort things — the first step in noticing differences.

parent.learn: Things in nature have usual colours: sky blue, leaves green, banana yellow.
parent.why: Knowing these lets the child spot when something has changed — a brown leaf is dry, a black banana is old.

parent.learn: Mixing colours makes new ones: red + yellow = orange, blue + yellow = green, red + blue = purple.
parent.why: Paints mix because each one carries its colour into the mixture — the child can see it happen with watercolours.

ask: Find something red in the room. Now something green.
Mix a little blue and yellow paint (or crayons). What colour comes?
What colour is the sky at night?
What colours are in a rainbow?

rounds.h: Red like a tomato or a fire engine.
Yellow like the sun or a banana.

rounds.t: What colour is the sky on a sunny day?
rounds.h: On a clear sunny day the sky is blue.

rounds.t: What colour is a ripe banana?
What colour is a ripe tomato?

rounds.h: Purple like a brinjal or grapes.

rounds.t: Red and yellow mixed together make…
rounds.h: Red and yellow paint make orange — like the colour of an orange!

rounds.t: Blue and yellow mixed together make…
rounds.h: Blue and yellow paint make green.

rounds.t: Red and blue mixed together make…
rounds.h: Red and blue paint make purple.

rounds.t: White and red mixed together make…
rounds.h: A little red in white makes pink.

rounds.t: Which colours does a traffic light have?
rounds.h: Red means stop, yellow means wait, green means go.
